description: Only examinations dated strictly between the two end dates are counted. Those dated exactly on either end date are left out.

d.request: Return the unrounded average ANA value (ignoring missing values) and count of examination records where Examination Date is strictly greater than 1995-11-09 and strictly less than 1997-03-17, as one row with average first and count second.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA), COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` > '1995-11-09' AND `Examination Date` < '1997-03-17'

b.request: For examinations with Examination Date strictly between 1995-11-09 and 1997-03-17 (excluding those dated exactly on either endpoint), return the unrounded average of non-null ANA values and the total number of examination records in one row.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA), COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` > '1995-11-09' AND `Examination Date` < '1997-03-17'
b.raw: For examinations with Examination Date strictly between 1995-11-09 and 1997-03-17 (excluding those dated exactly on either endpoint), return the unrounded average of non-null ANA values and the total number of examination records in one row.

a.request: Looking at examinations with an `Examination Date` strictly after 1995-11-09 and strictly before 1997-03-17 (comparing the dates as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give the answer as a single row with the unrounded average first and the record count second.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA) as average_ana, COUNT(*) as record_count FROM Examination WHERE CAST(`Examination Date` AS CHAR) > '1995-11-09' AND CAST(`Examination Date` AS CHAR) < '1997-03-17'

c.request: For examinations held between 1995-11-09 and 1997-03-17 (comparing the `Examination Date` as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give one row with the unrounded average first and the record count second. Only examinations dated strictly between the two end dates are counted. Those dated exactly on either end date are left out.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA) as average_ana, COUNT(*) as record_count FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` > '1995-11-09' AND `Examination Date` < '1997-03-17'
